questions.scenario: An application calls a model in a Microsoft Foundry project. The model was deployed with the deployment name support-chat. The application passes model="gpt-4.1-mini" and receives a DeploymentNotFound error.
questions.question: What should you change?

options.text: Pass support-chat as the model value
options.why: Correct. Calls are made to the deployment name.

options.text: Deploy a second copy of gpt-4.1-mini under the model name
options.why: Deployment names are chosen by you, and the application must use the one that exists.

options.text: Increase the tokens-per-minute quota
options.why: Quota limits throughput. It does not cause a missing deployment error.

options.text: Switch the application to an API key
options.why: The authentication method does not affect whether the deployment name is found.

questions.explanation: The model parameter carries the deployment name. The deployment holds the model, version, deployment type and capacity.

questions.scenario: A company must label 200,000 short support tickets each day as billing, delivery or other. The labels are simple, and cost and latency matter more than deep reasoning.
questions.question: Which model should you deploy for this task?

options.text: An image generation model such as gpt-image-1
options.why: Image generation models do not classify text.

options.text: A small language model such as Phi-4-mini-instruct
options.why: Correct. Simple, high-volume classification is a good fit for a small model.

options.text: A reasoning model such as o4-mini
options.why: Reasoning models cost more and respond more slowly than the task needs.

options.text: An embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small
options.why: Embedding models return vectors, not text labels.

questions.explanation: Match model size to the task. A small language model handles simple volume work cheaply and quickly, and a large or reasoning model is kept for hard problems.

questions.question: A Python application must connect to a Microsoft Foundry project by using the Foundry SDK. Which value does AIProjectClient require?

options.text: The connection string of a storage account
options.why: A storage connection string does not identify a Foundry project.

options.text: The name of the model in the catalog
options.why: The model name is not an endpoint. The app passes a deployment name when it calls a model.

options.text: The project endpoint
options.why: Correct. The endpoint has the form https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>.

options.text: The subscription ID of the resource group
options.why: The client needs the project endpoint, not the subscription ID.

questions.explanation: AIProjectClient takes the project endpoint and a credential, for example DefaultAzureCredential.

questions.scenario: An application runs on Azure Container Apps and calls a Foundry model deployment. Security policy forbids storing API keys.
questions.question: Which two actions should you perform? Select two.

options.text: Assign a Foundry role such as Foundry User to that identity on the Foundry resource
options.why: Correct. The identity must have a role that allows it to call the deployment.

options.text: Store the resource key in an environment variable
options.why: This stores a secret, which the policy forbids.

options.text: Create a second deployment for each user
options.why: Deployments are not used for authentication.

options.text: Enable a managed identity on the container app
options.why: Correct. The identity lets the app request Microsoft Entra ID tokens.

questions.explanation: Keyless access combines a managed identity with a role assignment, and the code uses DefaultAzureCredential.

questions.scenario: Customers upload photos of damaged parcels, and the app must describe the damage in text.
questions.question: Which type of model should you deploy?

options.text: A multimodal chat model that accepts image input, such as gpt-4.1
options.why: Correct. It can read an image and return a text description.

options.text: A text-only small language model
options.why: It cannot interpret image input.

options.text: An embedding model
options.why: It produces vectors and does not describe images.

options.text: A text-to-speech voice
options.why: Text to speech converts text into audio.

questions.explanation: Choose the model by input and output types. Image understanding requires a model that accepts images.
